page.overview:
Who is Kelsey?

Kelsey is the tritagonist of The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. He's a new teen at Devon and Mick's high school who makes friends with everyone, although seemingly prefers being around the two outcasts. Depending on how one interprets the story, Kelsey could be considered the main antagonist.

Kelsey is good-looking with wavy blond hair, blue eyes, straight teeth, and broad shoulders. He usually wears jeans torn at the knees and a watch. On his first day of school, he's wearing cool ripped jeans and a faded black T-shirt. The next day, he wears baggy black pants with a gray T-shirt and a black-and-red plaid shirt tied at his waist.

Kelsey is a very friendly, funny, and charismatic person, which allows him to make friends easily. He is also very observant, constantly evaluating people. Kelsey is very keen on justice, believing it to balance the scales by removing the downside so it can’t outweigh the upside. He likes legal shows and courtroom dramas, claiming to want to be a “real judge” someday. Kelsey also enjoys urban exploring. Despite Heather’s clear interest in him, Kelsey gets rather annoyed by her and her friend group interrupting his plans, although he never raises any objections and simply lets them derail the plan.

Kelsey starts his first day at his new school hanging out near the stairs and watching as other kids enter the school, including Devon. Kelsey manages to become friends with many of the kids at his school, including Mick. Mick properly introduces Devon to Kelsey and they begin to hang out together during lunch. The next day, Mick explains to Kelsey what happened to their old clubhouse. Kelsey promises the pair he will let them use a workshop at a farmhouse his parents purchased for their hangout. The next day, in their social studies class, the topic of justice is discussed. Kelsey explains that justice is something that removes the downs so it doesn't outweigh the ups. Heather, a pretty popular girl that Kelsey was getting along with, views justice as payback, and when asked if payback goes too far simply says that accidents happen. Only Mick and Kelsey don't find the joke funny.
